reference_notes.quality_bar_from_compass: Compass's buildSystemPrompt gives ~210 lines of behavioral guidance on top of injected live state: named disambiguation rules stated as explicit contrasts (pause_task vs cancel_task with example phrases on each side), explicit 'USE THE TOOL, don't just describe what you'd do', fuzzy-matching instructions with a ONE-clarifying-question fallback, per-domain worked scenarios, and explicit reasoning instructions for messy real-world signals. Codex's old dispatchSystemPrompt was 3 classification bullets + 4 path bullets with NO worked examples.
reference_notes.what_changed_vs_compass_lesson: The lesson taken from Compass was DEPTH AND SPECIFICITY (named contrasts, worked borderline examples on both sides, explicit weak-signal warnings), not literal content — Codex is a notebook, not a task manager. The pause-vs-cancel equivalent for Codex is note-vs-instruction, now stated as an explicit named rule with contrasting worked examples.

fixes.change_detail: dispatchSystemPrompt(tree) expanded from 3 classification bullets + 4 path bullets to a Compass-standard prompt: (1) named NOTE vs INSTRUCTION vs MESSAGE-TO-YOU three-way rule decided by 'what the user would want to HAPPEN, never by grammar alone'; (2) explicit 'grammatical mood is a WEAK signal' rule with both directions (questions can be notes, imperatives can be notes, declaratives can be instructions); (3) 9 worked examples of borderline phrasings on both sides; (4) explicit messy-transcript rule (filler words/false starts/run-ons never by themselves push toward file_note); (5) entry-preview content-targeting rule for content-described reads; (6) USE-THE-TOOL reinforcement. file_note's tool description tightened: 'Use ONLY for content the user wants kept... This is NOT a fallback for unclear messages.' Live tree injection and the 4 original deepest-node path-targeting bullets kept verbatim.
